'''Hunter Snevily''' (1956&ndash;2013) was an American [[mathematician]] with expertise and contributions in [[Set theory]], [[Graph theory]], [[Discrete geometry]], and [[Ramsey theory]] on the integers.<ref name=remem>
{{
cite journal
| last1 = Ahmed | first1 = Tanbir
| last2 = Kézdy | first2 = André
| last3 = West | first3 = Douglas | author3-link = Douglas West (mathematician) 
| title= Remembering Hunter Snevily
| journal = Bulletin of the [[Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications]]
| volume = 73
| year = 2015
| pages = 7–17
| mr=3331369
}}
</ref>

==Education and career==
Hunter received his undergraduate degree from [[Emory University]] in 1981,<ref name=obit/> and his Ph.D. degree from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] under the supervision of [[Douglas West (mathematician)|Douglas West]] in 1991.<ref name=obit/><ref name=mgp>{{Citation|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=4896|title=Hunter Snevily}}  at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref> After a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Caltech]], where he mentored many students, Hunter took a faculty position at the [[University of Idaho]] in 1993 where he was a professor until 2010.<ref name=obit/> He retired early <ref name=retire>
{{Cite web|url=https://www.uidaho.edu/-/media/UIdaho-Responsive/Files/sci/mathstat/news/newsletters/math-news-2011.pdf |title=Hunter Snevily retires|date=2022-10-22}}
</ref> while fighting with [[Parkinsons]],<ref name=obit/><ref name=remem/> but continued research in mathematics till his last days.<ref name=obit/><ref name=remem/>

==Mathematics research==
The following are some of Hunter's most important contributions (as discussed in <ref name=remem />):
* Hunter formulated a conjecture (1991) <ref name=thesis>
{{
cite journal
| last = Snevily | first = Hunter 
| title = Combinatorics of Finite Sets
| journal = [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]
| year = 1991
}}
</ref> bounding the size of a family of sets under intersection constraints. He conjectured that if <math>{\mathcal L}</math> is a set of <math>k</math> positive integers and <math>\{A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_m\}</math> is a family of subsets of an <math>n</math>-set satisfying <math>|A_i \cap A_j| \in {\mathcal L}</math> whenever <math>i \neq j</math>, then <math>m \leq \sum_{i=0}^k{n-1 \choose i}</math>. His conjecture was ambitious in a way it would beautifully unify classical results of [[Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn]] and [[Paul Erdős]] (1948),<ref name=dberdos>
{{
cite journal
| last1 = de Bruijn | first1 = Nicolaas G. | author1-link = Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn
| last2 = Erdős | first2 = Paul | author2-link =  Paul Erdős
| title = On a Combinatorial Problem
| journal = Indagationes Mathematicae
| volume = 10
| year = 1948
| pages = 421–423
}}
</ref> Bose (1949),<ref name=bose>
{{
cite journal
| last = Bose | first = R. C.
| title = A note on Fisher's inequality for balanced incomplete block designs
| journal = [[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]
| volume = 20
| year = 1949
| issue = 4
| pages = 619–620
| doi = 10.1214/aoms/1177729958
| doi-access = free
}}
</ref> Majumdar (1953),<ref name=majumder>
{{
cite journal
| last = Majumdar | first = K. N.
| title = On some theorems in combinatorics relating to incomplete block designs
| journal = [[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]
| volume = 24
| year = 1953
| issue = 3
| pages = 377–389
| doi = 10.1214/aoms/1177728978
| doi-access = free
}}
</ref> [[H. J. Ryser]] (1968),<ref name=ryser>
{{
cite journal
| last = Ryser | first = H. J. | author1-link = H. J. Ryser
| title = An extension of a theorem of de bruijn and Erdős on combinatorial designs
| journal = [[Journal of Algebra]]
| volume = 10
| year = 1968
| issue = 2 | pages = 246–261
| doi = 10.1016/0021-8693(68)90099-9 | doi-access = free
}}
</ref> Frankl and Füredi (1981),<ref name=ff>
{{
cite journal
| last1 = Frankl | first1 = P. 
| last2 = Füredi | first2 = Zoltán | author2-link = Zoltán Füredi 
| title = Families of finite sets with a missing intersection
| journal = Proc. Colloq. Math. Soc. Janos Bolyai (Eger, Hungary)
| volume = 37
| year = 1981
| pages = 305–318
}}
</ref> and Frankl and Wilson (1981).<ref name=fw>
{{
cite journal
| last1 = Frankl | first1 = P. 
| last2 = Wilson | first2 = R. M.

| journal = [[Combinatorica]]

| issue = 3
| year = 2003
| pages = 527–533
| doi = 10.1007/s00493-003-0031-2 
| s2cid = 20035419 
}}
</ref>
* Hunter made important contribution to the well known [[Chvátal's Conjecture]] (1974)<ref name=chvatal_conj>
{{
cite conference
| last = Chvátal | first = V. | author1-link = Václav Chvátal
| title= Unsolved Problem No. 7. Hypergraph Seminar (Proc. First Working Sem., Ohio State Univ., Columbus, Ohio, 1972)
| series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics
| volume = 411
| year = 1974
| pages = Springer, Berlin
}}
</ref> which states that every hereditary family <math>{\mathcal F}</math> of sets has a largest intersecting subfamily consisting of sets with a common element. Schönheim<ref name=schon>
{{
cite journal
| last = Schönheim | first = J. 
| title = Hereditary systems and Chvátal's conjecture, in: Proceedings of the Fifth British Combinatorial Conference (Univ. Aberdeen, Aberdeen, 1975)
| journal = Congressus Numerantium
| volume = XV
| year = 1976
| pages = 537–539
}}
</ref> proved this when the maximal members of <math>{\mathcal F}</math> have a common element. [[Vašek Chvátal]] proved it when there is a linear order on the elements such that <math>\{b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_k\}\in{\mathcal F}</math> implies <math>\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k\}\in{\mathcal F}</math> when <math>a_i \leq b_i</math> for <math>1 \leq i \leq k</math>. A family <math>{\mathcal F}</math> has <math>x</math> as a dominant element if substituting <math>x</math> for any element of a member of <math>{\mathcal F}</math> not containing <math>x</math> yields another member of <math>{\mathcal F}</math>. Hunter's 1992 result<ref name=hunter1992>
{{
cite journal
| last = Snevily | first = Hunter 
| title = A New Result on Chvátal's Conjecture
| journal = [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | series=Series A
| volume = 61
| year = 1992
| pages = 137–141
| doi = 10.1016/0097-3165(92)90059-4 
| doi-access = free
}}
</ref> greatly strengthened both Schönheim's result and Chvátal's result by proving the conjecture for all families having a dominant element; it was major progress on the problem.

{{Cite web | url = https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=Snevily%2C+Hunter | title = Hunter Snevily | date = 2022-10-18}} in [[ZbMATH Open]]
</ref> is with [[Lior Pachter]] and Bill Voxman<ref name=pebble>{{cite conference

 | series = Congressus Numerantium
 | title = Proceedings of the Twenty-Sixth Southeastern International Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (Boca Raton, FL, 1995)
 | volume = 107
 | year = 1995
 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151125194114/https://math.berkeley.edu/~lpachter/papers/pebble.pdf
 | archive-date=2015-11-25}}
</ref> on [[Graph pebbling]]. This paper and Hunter's later paper<ref name=foster>
{{
cite journal
| last1 = Snevily | first1 = Hunter

| issue = 2
| pages = 231–244
| doi = 10.1007/PL00021179
| s2cid = 12095903
}}
</ref> with Foster added several conjectures on the subject and together have been cited in more than 50 papers.

* One of Hunter's conjectures (1999)<ref name=conj1999>
{{
cite journal
| last = Snevily
| first = Hunter
| title= Unsolved Problems: The Cayley Addition Table of <math>{\mathbb Z}_n</math>
| journal = [[American Mathematical Monthly]]
| volume = 106
| issue = 6
| year = 1999
| pages = 584–585
}}
</ref> became known as Snevily's Conjecture:<ref name=sc>
{{cite web | url = https://groupprops.subwiki.org/wiki/Snevily%27s_conjecture | title= Snevily's conjecture | date = 2022-10-21}}
</ref> Given an [[abelian group]] <math>G</math> of odd order, and subsets <math>\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k\}</math> and <math>\{b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_k\}</math> of <math>G</math>, there exists a [[permutation]] <math>\pi</math> of <math>[k]</math> such that <math>a_1+b_{\pi}(1), a_2+b_{\pi}(2), \ldots, a_k+b_{\pi}(k)</math> are distinct. [[Noga Alon]]<ref name=alon2000>
{{
cite journal
| last = Alon | first = Noga | author1-link = Noga Alon
| title= Additive Latin transversals
| journal = [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume = 117
| year = 2000
| pages = 125–130
| doi = 10.1007/BF02773567 | s2cid = 16047303 }}
</ref> proved this for [[cyclic group]]s of prime order. Dasgupta et al. (2001).<ref name=dasgupta>
{{
cite journal
| last1 = Dasgupta
| first1 = S.
| last2 = Karolyi
| first2 = Gy.
| last3 = Serra
| first3 = O.
| last4 = Szegedy
| first4 = B.
| title= Transversals of additive Latin squares
| journal = [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume = 126
| year = 2001
| pages = 17–28
| doi = 10.1007/BF02784149
| s2cid = 17826107
}}
</ref> proved it for all cyclic groups. Finally, after a decade, the conjecture was proved for all groups by a young mathematician Arsovski.<ref name=arsovski2011>
{{
cite journal
| last = Arsovski
| first = Bodan
| title= A proof of Snevily's Conjecture
| journal = [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume = 182
| year = 2011
| pages = 505–508
| doi = 10.1007/s11856-011-0040-6
| s2cid = 119529990
}}
</ref> [[Terence Tao]] devoted a section to Snevily's Conjecture in his well-known book [[Additive Combinatorics]].
